thesis: Dell's 60-day +31% move and 52-week high ($595.51, set 2026-09-18) are driven by a confirmed, company-specific catalyst: Q2 FY27 earnings (2026-09-01) beat on revenue (+58% YoY) and EPS, with record $60.9B in AI server orders and a $95B backlog. thesis: SPCX's 60-day +32% move reflects a stack of confirmed, company-specific catalysts -- a ~$950M NASA ISS-flights award, an AI-compute hosting contract, and expanded Space Force contract activity -- layered with real momentum and Nasdaq-100-rebalancing flows plus analyst price-target optimism that is opinion, not fact. invalidation: the maintenance-dosing benefit doesn't hold up in the pivotal Phase 3 data (2027), or a large ATM-funded raise executes at a material discount

thesis: AXT's Q2 2026 return to profit (revenue +164% YoY, record $100M InP backlog) and funded capacity expansion are real, confirmed fundamentals supporting the AI-optics demand story. Layered on top: a GuruFocus quant model flags the stock near 20x its estimated fair value, directors have sold ~$78.8M in stock over the trailing year with zero insider buying, and an unresolved (but not court-scheduled) securities suit alleges data/compliance issues at the Chinese operating subsidiary. None of these meet the strict risk_flags definitions (no scheduled litigation date; the April 2026 offering falls outside the 90-day dilution_risk window), but together they're mixed enough evidence to justify low rather than higher conviction.
invalidation: insider selling accelerates further, the unresolved securities litigation produces an adverse ruling, or Q3 earnings (est. 2026-10-29) show the growth reversing
